summary: OpenCode 2.x through the existing ACP adapter, behind the staged flag opencode_v2_acp (OPENCODE_V2_ACP_ENABLED, false; SB_OPENCODE_V2_ACP=1 in Switchboard's env turns it on for testing). With the flag off nothing changes except the refusal copy, which now tells a user who ran `opencode upgrade --major` how to put 1.x back (npm i -g opencode-ai@1 or the curl installer) and that 2.x moved their sign-ins into its database. With the flag on, assertSupportedOpencode returns the generation (1 or 2) instead of refusing a 2.x (3.x and later are still refused, an unversioned install with a v2 signal counts as 2), and every spawn site follows it: the chat adapter and the native-fork runner start `opencode acp` with no --cwd (the spawn cwd is the folder), and the catalog probe and the Settings Test run `opencode models --standalone`, so a private server gets the account's env instead of the shared background service. Model changes already went through setSessionConfigOption whenever session/new returns a model config option; now, once the agent reports an effort option (or the preflight names one for 2.x), a provider/model/variant pick is split into the model option and the effort option (the base level is `default`), and model.variants is emitted from the effort option, so the composer's effort control works as with 1.x. A 1.x session, which reports no effort option, keeps its model ids whole and gets no new event. A subagent's text that 2.x streams into the parent session (_meta opencode/child-session) is dropped so it does not run into the parent's message; its tool calls still show.

desktop.followUpRelease: The release that sets OPENCODE_V2_ACP_ENABLED to true, after a 2.x chat is checked with a signed-in provider: approval cards for a code-mode execute call, the question tool (it fails over ACP on 2.x and the adapter has no question handling for OpenCode), and subagent tool calls shown under their subagent row. What ships now: the refusal copy for everyone, and the whole v2 path for anyone who sets SB_OPENCODE_V2_ACP=1.

reactNativeIos.reason: The adapter, the version gate, the catalog probe, the fork runner and the Settings Test all run on the backend. A phone reads OpenCode models through LIST_MODELS and variants through the existing model.variants event, both unchanged in shape, and shows a refusal as the existing start-session error text.

nativeAndroid.reason: Same as React Native: everything changed runs on the backend, and Android gets the same model.variants event and start-session error string it already handles. No Android code or wire field changed.

sharedBackendApi.followUpRelease: Same release as the desktop entry: the headless server runs the same main-process code and the same flag.

storageDataMigration.reason: Nothing Switchboard stores changed: no schema, migration or setting. With the flag on, a 2.x binary runs, and 2.x migrates the user's own opencode.db forward in place and moves auth.json into it. That is OpenCode's own one-way upgrade, which the user started with `opencode upgrade --major` or a 2.x install; the flag only lets Switchboard drive a binary the user already chose.

updateRelease.reason: No package identity, signing, native module, deep link or release packaging changed. The flag is a compile-time constant (off) plus an env override, so a release ships the 1.x-only behaviour.
